points.why: It opens by calling the pattern of five differently caused outages at an unchanged rate the real finding, which points to conditions rather than triggers.
It lines the incidents up as one dataset and asks what structure lets them through, but it never asks what mental model keeps that structure in place beyond questioning single-root-cause thinking.
It names shared, unchanged factors such as pressure to ship, on-call overload, deprioritized reliability work and unclear ownership as conditions that let any trigger become an outage.

pitfalls.why: It proposes class-level controls as a hypothesis to test across incidents, not another single root-cause fix, though its list of technical remedies leans that way.

notes: Its main hypothesis and remedies stay technical (change safety, degradation, detection), with organizational structure as a late add-on, so it risks becoming a bundle of technical fixes.
